text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Lebanon's Banque du Liban et d'Outre Mer said it had doubled its capital to $150 million and it had acquired all shares in Banque Banorabe-France which also fully owns Banque Banorient-Suisse.

-The council of the Christian Maronite Bishops denounces the bus explosion in Damascus and the attack on the Syrian van in Tabarja north of Beirut and says "the authorities had confused revenge and reform during its campaign of arrests."
-An investigating judge ruled that the Solidere company will not face trial over the deaths of 14 people in a 1996 building collapse which occured in central Beirut area that Solidere is rebuilding.
-A five-nation group monitoring a ceasefire understanding in south Lebanon urged Hizbollah guerrillas and Israeli forces to stay clear of civilian areas in their tit-for-tat war.
-one Israeli soldier was killed and nine wounded in various guerrilla attacks inside the Israeli south Lebanon occupation zone and Katyusha rocket slammed into Israel.
-Israeli warplanes raid the Iqlim al-Toufah ridge thee times and Israeli gunners pound the area with heavy shelling.
-Foreign Minister Bouez, after meeting his Syrian countepart al-Shara, accused Israel of increasing tension in south Lebanon and trying to undermine security in both Syria and Lebanon.
-Economy ministry plans to buy 50,000 tonnes of U.S. hard wheat later this month on the international market, an official of the Cereals and Sugar Beet Office said.
-Six lebanese men were arrested in Germany for trying to enter the country illegally.
-Prime Minister Hariri says "war with Israel is out of the question because it is not an easy matter and it hurts everybody".
